info.title: WideCast.ai Public API
info.summary: Turn plain-text scripts into AI-generated short-form videos.
info.description:
WideCast.ai turns plain-text scripts (and soon ideas, audio, existing videos)
into AI-generated short-form videos: scenes + voice + B-roll, ready for
review in the scene editor.

**Authentication**: every request needs an API key, passed as
`Authorization: Bearer wc_live_*`. Generate keys in the dashboard
(Setup Center → API Keys). Each call to `/v1/create_video` consumes
credits from your account; usage (calls + credits) is tracked per key.

## Two input flows (`source`) × two completion gates (`output_type`)

### `source` — what kind of input you provide

1. **`source: "text"`** (default) — you provide `script_text` (80-500
   words), used VERBATIM by the narrator. No AI rewriting.
2. **`source: "idea"`** — you provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words, longer
   gets auto-truncated). The server writes a narration from the idea
   (AI), then continues the same scene-sourcing flow as `text`. You
   also pick `language`, `video_length` (short/normal), and
   `research_enabled`.
3. **`source: "blog"`** — you provide `blog_text` (30-3000 words — an
   article to repurpose; longer auto-truncated). Identical pipeline to
   `idea` (same AI script-writer), just a longer input. Same optional
   `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative sources**: the server writes the script
first (Phase 1), so they support `output_type: "text"` to stop at the
editable script. Future generative sources (audio, video) follow the
same shape.

### `output_type` — how far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth)

1. **`output_type: "text"`** — stop after the source→script-text phase.
   Returns a `review_url` (the UI auto-detects the data is narration-only
   and opens the Script Editor). **Only valid for generative sources**
   (`source != "text"`) — for `source: "text"` you already supplied the
   script, so `text` output would echo your input (HTTP 400).
2. **`output_type: "scene"`** (default) — stop at "scenes ready for
   review". You get back a `review_url` to inspect / edit before deciding
   to render the final MP4. Optional follow-up: `POST /v1/export_video`.
3. **`output_type: "video"`** — run end-to-end without manual review.
   `result.video_url` populated when the final MP4 is ready. Use this
   when you trust the generated scenes (programmatic / batch use).

The two axes combine — every valid `source` × `output_type` pair works,
except `source: "text"` + `output_type: "text"` (rejected — see above).

## Endpoints

- **POST `/v1/create_video`** — submit `script_text`/`idea_text` + optional
  `output_type`. Returns a `widecast*` id and initial `status: "processing"`.
- **POST `/v1/export_video`** — for `output_type: "scene"` videos that
  reached `scenes_ready_for_review`, kick the final-MP4 renderer.
  Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op.
- **GET `/v1/status/{id}`** — poll until `status` is `completed` (or
  `failed`). `result.review_url` is present from the first response
  (`pending`/`processing` too) — it's a stable id-keyed page, so you can
  show it to the user immediately. The completion gate depends on the
  video's `output_type`:
    * text  → `stage: "script_ready_for_review"`.
    * scene → `stage: "scenes_ready_for_review"`.
    * video → `stage: "video_rendered"`, `result.video_url` also set.

Polling cadence: start at 5s, exponential backoff (×1.5) up to 60s. The
SDKs implement this automatically via `video.wait()`.

## Script bounds (LOCKED)

`script_text` is used **verbatim** by the narrator — no rewriting. The
bounds reflect what fits inside a short-form video:

- **Minimum 80 words** (~20s of narration) — anything shorter renders
  a useless clip.
- **Maximum 500 words** (~120s / 2 min of narration) — beyond this,
  render cost and pacing both suffer.

## Inline media in `script_text`

Drop a **direct image or video URL** into the script next to the line it
should illustrate — WideCast strips it from the narration and uses it as
that scene's visual instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Two equivalent forms:

* **Markdown image syntax** (recommended for AI-chat callers):
  `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg)`. Chat
  hosts (Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini) render the picture inline so
  the user can SEE whether the visual fits the narration before
  approving the script. The alt text doubles as the strongest possible
  scene anchor.
* **Raw URL** on its own line (works the same; backward-compatible):
  `Our cold brew steeps for 16 hours. https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg
  That mellow finish is what people come back for.`

Direct file links only (image `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp/.avif/.svg`,
video `.mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.avi`); page links like a YouTube watch URL
are not inlined (use `source="video_url"` for those). See the
`script_text` field for details.

## Field-requirement convention (LOCKED)

Every constraint on every field — validation bounds, enum values,
required-vs-optional, defaults — appears in **four places**, kept in
sync:

1. **OpenAPI spec** — `description`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum`,
   `default`. Single source devs read first.
2. **SDK constants + types** — named exports in `widecast` (Python) and
   `@widecast/sdk` (TypeScript), so callers can refer to them
   programmatically without re-typing the literal.
3. **Markdown docs** — `Field reference` table in each endpoint page.
4. **Server enforcement** — rejected requests must surface a LOCKED
   `error.code` (e.g. `script_too_short`, `invalid_output_type`).

The SDK parity test (`test_script_bounds_constants_locked` and
equivalents) imports each SDK constant and asserts the exact numeric
value — changing one surface without the others breaks the test. New
endpoints MUST follow this same pattern.

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- Snake_case JSON fields
- **ID format**: `widecast<alphanumeric>` (~20 chars). The server's new-script
  detection checks for the literal `"widecast"` substring, so SDKs/clients MUST
  not strip it. Public id == internal `topic_id` (1:1, no mapping).
- API key prefixes: `wc_live_*`
- Object marker: every resource has `"object": "<type>"`
- Status enum: `pending | processing | completed | failed`
  (`pending` ONLY covers the brief race window between create + worker
  writing the topic row; once the row exists, status is `processing` —
  the abroll worker doesn't increment `step` until the end)
- Error envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?",
  "doc_url", "request_id" } }`
- Error codes (v0.1.0): `account_expired | credit_exhausted |
  render_failed | unknown_error | scenes_not_ready | export_failed |
  script_too_short | script_too_long | invalid_output_type |
  invalid_source | idea_too_short | missing_idea_text |
  blog_too_short | missing_blog_text |
  missing_video_url | missing_audio_url | missing_media_file |
  unsupported_media_url | media_too_long | file_too_large |
  missing_api_key | invalid_api_key |
  invalid_language | invalid_video_length | invalid_research_enabled |
  invalid_faceless | invalid_content_type | invalid_intervention_level |
  ideas_failed | invalid_publish_input | invalid_platforms |
  no_platforms_connected | publish_not_ready | download_failed |
  publish_failed | free_tier_limit_exceeded | telegram_not_connected |
  telegram_send_failed | invalid_parse_mode | conflicting_media |
  invalid_photo_url | invalid_video_url | message_too_long |
  rate_limited`
- Headers (every response): `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`,
  `X-WideCast-Version`
- Timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC strings (e.g. `2026-05-19T17:30:00Z`)
- Pagination (future): cursor-based — see `ListEnvelope` schema

tags.description:
Documented OUT-of-band — WideCast does NOT define a webhook endpoint on
its own server; the client supplies a `callback_url` in `POST /v1/create_video`,
and WideCast POSTs events to that URL. See the WebhookEvent schema below
for the payload + the `WebhookEvent.event_type` enum for fire-points.

Client-generated UUID. Two requests with the same key within 24h return
the SAME video and do NOT create a new one. **Read but not enforced
in pilot.**

value.script_text: Want to make a video in 60 seconds? Here's how — and why it actually works. First, draft your script in bullet points. Don't overthink it. Three to five beats is plenty: a hook that grabs attention, a body that delivers one clear idea, and a call to action that tells the viewer exactly what to do next. Second, paste it into WideCast and pick an aspect ratio. Vertical for TikTok and Reels, square for feed posts. Third, hit render and grab a coffee. The AI does the work. You come back to a video that's ready to publish. Try it free at widecast.ai today.

Behind the wheel is where they learn to make decisions in real time, manage risk, and own the consequences of their own choices. The longer you delay, the harder it gets. Don't make your kid that twenty-two-year-old learning under pressure. Let them get the license now.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Which writing skill to load.
* `video` — short-form video script (TikTok / Reels / Shorts /
  YouTube short). Pairs with `createVideo source='text'`.
* `blog` — article / SEO post / long-form. Pairs with
  `createVideo source='blog'` (repurpose-to-video).
* `social` — platform caption (X / LinkedIn / IG / TikTok / FB /
  Threads). Pairs with `createVideo source='idea'` if the user
  wants a video version.

XRequestId.description: Unique ID for this request — include in any support ticket.

CreateVideoRequest.description:
Conditional shape based on `source`:
  * source="text" (default) → `script_text` required.
  * source="idea" → `idea_text` required; `language`, `video_length`,
    `research_enabled` optional with defaults.
The other text field is ignored when not matching `source`.

script_approved.description:
Confirmation flag for AI agents calling via MCP or ChatGPT Action.
**MCP callers**: REQUIRED (the MCP wrapper rejects calls where this
is missing or false). **ChatGPT Action callers**: should set true
after showing the user the full hand-off and getting explicit
approval. **SDK / curl / Postman callers**: this field is ignored
by the REST endpoint; SDK consumers are trusted to handle their
own UX. The point of the flag is to enforce that the dialog flow
with the end user actually happened — a bare "make a video about X"
from the user is the REQUEST, not the approval.

production_mode.description:
User's explicit answer to the three-way production question.
Applies to source=text/idea/blog AND source=audio_url
(ignored for video sources — the footage IS the visuals).
Three valid values, each with a different downstream UX:
  * `faceless` — B-roll only, no narrator on screen. The video
    is fully automated; user just reviews and renders.
  * `face_clone` — the user's pre-trained Face clone + Voice
    clone speaks the script. The user **must have set both up
    at https://widecast.ai/#setup** before the render runs —
    if they haven't, the AI agent should point them there
    during the dialog.
  * `teleprompter` — the user records themselves reading the
    script via WideCast's built-in teleprompter (after the
    scenes prepare). No clone needed; user physically records.
Both `face_clone` and `teleprompter` produce a "normal" video
(narrator on screen) and map to the legacy `faceless=false`
on the REST endpoint — the distinction is purely so the AI
agent tells the user the right next step.
**Audio-source nuance** (source=audio_url): the user's original
voice in the recording IS the narration in every mode — it is
never re-synthesized via TTS. `face_clone` here means the clone's
face is on screen lip-synced to the user's original audio (not
to a clone-voice resynthesis); the clone contributes only the
visual face, the voice stays the user's.
**MCP / Action callers**: pass the user's answer here; the MCP
wrapper performs the mapping. **SDK / curl callers**: skip this
field, set `faceless` directly as before.

source.description:
Discriminates the input flow:
  * `text` (default — backward-compat): provide `script_text`
    used VERBATIM by the narrator.
  * `idea`: provide `idea_text`; server writes a narration from
    the idea (AI) then continues into the same scene-sourcing
    pipeline as `text`.
  * `blog`: provide `blog_text` (an article to repurpose);
    identical pipeline to `idea`, just a longer input.
  * `video_url` / `audio_url`: provide `video_url` / `audio_url`
    — **any public http(s) URL**. Direct file links (S3, R2,
    transfer.sh, file.io, your own CDN — anywhere an AI agent or
    user can drop the file and copy back a URL) AND platform pages
    (YouTube / TikTok / Facebook) both work. Loopback / private /
    link-local hosts are rejected (`unsupported_media_url`).
    Media-ingest (A49) — the script already lives in the media.
    The footage becomes the B-roll (video) / the audio becomes
    the narration (audio).
  * `video_file` / `audio_file`: upload the media file. Send the
    request as **multipart/form-data** with the file in the
    `video_file` / `audio_file` part (mirrors the UI upload).
**AI agent path for "user attached a file in chat":** call
`POST /v1/upload_asset` first (or the MCP `widecast_upload_asset`
tool), get back a public S3 URL with a 24-hour TTL, then pass
that URL here as `audio_url` / `video_url`. Do NOT inline-base64.
`idea` and `blog` are generative sources — they support
`output_type: "text"` (stop at the editable script). Media sources
support `output_type: "text"` too = Remake (A50): extract the
transcript only, no footage/scene build.

script_text.description:
**Required when `source="text"`.** Plain text script — pasted
narration. Used VERBATIM by the narrator (no AI rewriting).
Bounds are LOCKED:
  * minimum 80 words (~20s of narration)
  * maximum 500 words (~120s / 2 min of narration)

Word count = whitespace split (`len(text.split())`) — works for
English + Vietnamese. Outside the bounds → HTTP 400 with
`error.code` = `script_too_short` / `script_too_long`.

**Inline media (use your own images/videos).** You can drop a
direct image or video URL straight into the script, right after
(or before) the sentence it should illustrate. WideCast (1) strips
the URL (or markdown image construct) from the spoken narration
and (2) uses that asset as the visual for the matching scene,
instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Two equivalent forms — pick by
caller:

  * **Markdown image syntax** (recommended for AI-chat callers
    like Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini):
    `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg)`.
    Chat hosts render the picture inline so the end-user can
    visually approve each scene before the script is submitted.
    Alt text doubles as the strongest scene anchor.
  * **Raw URL** on its own line, surrounded by descriptive words
    (the v0.1.0 default; still works):
    `Our cold brew steeps for 16 hours.
    https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg That mellow finish…`.

Mix both freely. Supported = direct file links ending in an image
extension (`.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .bmp .avif .svg`) or video
extension (`.mp4 .webm .mov .m4v .avi`), optionally with a
`?query`. Page links (e.g. `https://youtube.com/watch?...`) are
NOT used as inline assets — to turn a whole YouTube/TikTok clip
into a video use `source="video_url"` instead. Keep a few
descriptive words (or alt text) next to the URL so it anchors to
the right scene; multiple URLs are supported; scenes without a
URL still get automatic B-roll.
script_text.example: California parents should encourage their teens to get a driver's license at 16. Driving builds independence, responsibility, and confidence — three things every teenager needs more of, and three things you can't teach from a couch...

idea_text.description:
**Required when `source="idea"`.** Short description of what you
want the video about. The server writes a narration from this
(AI) and continues into the scene-sourcing pipeline. Bounds:
  * minimum 5 words — `idea_too_short` if shorter.
  * maximum 1000 words — longer is auto-truncated at a whitespace
    boundary (NOT rejected). Original word count surfaces in
    `details.input_truncated_from` on `/v1/status`.

Word count = whitespace split.
idea_text.example: Why teens should get their driver's license at 16, not 18 — independence, responsibility, and stake-low practice.

blog_text.description:
**Required when `source="blog"`.** A blog post or article to
repurpose into a video. The server condenses it into a narration
(same AI script-writer as `idea`) then continues into the
scene-sourcing pipeline. Bounds:
  * minimum 30 words — `blog_too_short` if shorter (use
    `source=idea` for a one-liner brief instead).
  * maximum 3000 words — longer is auto-truncated at a whitespace
    boundary (NOT rejected). Original word count surfaces in
    `details.input_truncated_from` on `/v1/status`.

Word count = whitespace split.
blog_text.example: Every hurricane season, thousands of homeowners discover the same painful fact: their homeowner's insurance does not cover flood damage. Standard policies exclude rising-water damage entirely...

video_url.description:
**Required when `source="video_url"`.** A YouTube / TikTok /
Facebook video URL. The server downloads it, then the footage
becomes the B-roll (Auto-Edit). Non-allowed hosts → HTTP 400
`unsupported_media_url`; media over 5 minutes → `media_too_long`.

audio_url.description:
**Required when `source="audio_url"`.** A YouTube / TikTok /
Facebook URL whose audio becomes the narration (Audio-to-Video).
Same host allow-list + 5-minute cap as `video_url`.
**Voice handling**: the user's original voice in the audio is kept
verbatim as the narration in every production_mode (it is never
re-synthesized via TTS). If they pick `production_mode="face_clone"`,
the clone's face is lip-synced TO the user's original audio —
voice stays the user's, only the on-screen face is the clone.

video_file.description:
**Required when `source="video_file"`.** The video file, sent as
multipart/form-data. Caps: **≤ 100 MB** (`file_too_large`) and
**≤ 5 minutes** (`media_too_long`). Only present in the multipart
request variant.

audio_file.description:
**Required when `source="audio_file"`.** The audio file, sent as
multipart/form-data. Caps: **≤ 100 MB** (`file_too_large`) and
**≤ 5 minutes** (`media_too_long`). Only present in the multipart
request variant.

language.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
Narration language. v0.1.0 enum locked to English + Vietnamese.
Expanding requires a parity-test bump per A38.

video_length.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
Target video length. Maps to legacy `content_type` 9 / 10.
  * `short` — ~90 seconds of narration (content_type 9).
  * `normal` — longer-form, capped at ~3 minutes total
    (content_type 10).

research_enabled.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
If true, the AI runs research / fact-check during narration
generation. Default true (matches the UI's default-on behavior).
Disable only if you know your idea is self-contained and
doesn't need external facts.

output_type.description:
How far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth). For ALL three,
`result.review_url` ships in the create response itself (safe to
share with the user immediately — the page handles early arrival
with an in-page spinner). `video_url` is the field that gates on
completion (output_type=video / after export_video).
  * `text` — stops after the source→script-text phase.
    `review_url` opens the Script Editor.
    ONLY valid for generative sources (source != "text").
    source="text" + output_type="text" → HTTP 400
    `invalid_output_type` (you already supplied the script).
  * `scene` (default) — stops at scenes-ready-for-review.
    `review_url` opens the Scene Editor. Caller can then inspect /
    edit and call `POST /v1/export_video` to render the MP4 — or
    stop there.
  * `video` — auto-chains into the renderer once scenes are ready.
    `result.video_url` populated on completion. Use when you
    trust generated scenes.

faceless.description:
**Used when `output_type` is `scene` or `video`** for sources
text / idea / blog AND for audio sources (`audio_url` /
`audio_base64`) — the script comes from a text input OR from
transcribing the user's audio, but the visuals must still be
generated, so the same A/B-roll toggle applies. When `true`,
EVERY scene is rendered as B-roll (stock video / AI image) with
NO narrator A-roll anywhere — a "faceless" video. When `false`
(default), scenes mix narrator A-roll + B-roll as usual.
Rejected with HTTP 400 `invalid_faceless` when `output_type="text"`
(no scenes are produced) or for video sources (`video_url` /
`video_file` — the footage IS the visuals).

media_pool.description:
Optional list of **direct image/video file URLs** that aren't placed
inline in the script. WideCast downloads each (image → + thumbnail)
and adds them to the **first scene's** media library, so the scene
editor lists them and the user can drop any into any scene — no
separate media-picker step. Use for images you have but can't
confidently match to a beat (inline the ones you can). Best-effort:
applies on the scene-producing path (text/idea/blog, output_type
scene/video); ignored for output_type='text' / media sources. Same
rule as inline URLs: direct file links only, never fabricated.

wait_for_render.description:
If true, block up to 60s waiting for completion. If the deadline hits
before completion, return the in-flight state and let the client poll.

callback_url.description:
HTTPS URL that will receive a POST when the video completes or fails.
**Accepted but not delivered in pilot — see ROADMAP Phase 1 webhooks.**

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs stored alongside the video and echoed back on status. Max 16 keys, 500 chars each.

id.description:
`topic_id` returned by `/v1/create_video`. The video must have
reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 otherwise).

user_confirmed_render.description:
Confirmation flag for AI agents calling via MCP or ChatGPT Action.
**MCP callers**: REQUIRED (the MCP wrapper rejects calls where
this is missing or false). **ChatGPT Action callers**: should set
true after asking the user "Render the final video now, or do
you want to review the scenes first?" and getting an explicit
yes. **SDK / curl / Postman callers**: this field is ignored by
the REST endpoint. Each export is a new decision — never infer
from earlier in the conversation; even if the user wanted the
final video originally, ask again each time.

id.description:
`topic_id` from `/v1/create_video`. Same id used by `/v1/status`
and `/v1/export_video`. The video must have reached
`scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 otherwise).

by.description:
How to pick the scene.
  * `id` — exact match on `segment.id` (most reliable when
    /v1/status has given you one).
  * `voice_file` — exact match on the per-scene uid (also the
    mp3 narration filename).
  * `text` — fuzzy match against `segment.text`. If two scenes
    match too closely the response is a `ClarificationResponse`
    — pass `candidates` to the user and call again with
    `by="voice_file"`.

value.description: The id / voice_file string / narration snippet to match.

fields.description:
Edits to apply. Today honoured:
  * `{field_name: "mediaUrl", value: "<http(s) URL>"}` —
    background image OR video for this scene.
  * `{field_name: "mediaType", value: "image" | "video"}` —
    optional; auto-detected from the URL extension if omitted.
Other field names return `unsupported_field` (HTTP 400).

value.description: Any JSON value; for media edits, a string URL.

op.description:
Reserved for future generic field ops. Defaults to `set`. Ignored
for the current media-only edit path.

min_score.description:
Only when `by="text"`. Acceptance threshold for fuzzy match.
Lower it cautiously when the user paraphrased; raising past 0.9
usually causes false negatives because exact text rarely matches
verbatim.

ModifySceneRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/modify_scene. SYNCHRONOUS, no credit charged. On
ambiguous text match the response is a 200 `ClarificationResponse`
(with `candidates`) — no edit applied, retry with `by="voice_file"`.

SceneCandidate.description:
One ambiguous-match candidate returned when `by="text"` could not
decide between two or more scenes. Use `voice_file` (preferred) or
`segment_id` to call /v1/modify_scene again with `by="voice_file"`.

text.description: First ~80 chars of the scene's narration (preview).

scene_id.description: segment.id of the scene that was edited.

voice_file.description: voice_file uid of the edited scene.

score.description:
Resolution confidence (1.0 for `by="id"` and `by="voice_file"`;
the fuzzy score for `by="text"`).

applied.description: Which family of edits ran. Today only `media`.

media_type.description: Set when `applied="media"`. The resolved asset type.

AssetResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/upload_asset (multipart or JSON+base64). The
`url` is publicly reachable (S3 anonymous-read), valid for **24
hours** before the bucket lifecycle rule on the `assets/` prefix
deletes the object.

url.description: Public S3 URL — pass into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or use as an inline `![](url)` in script_text.

content_type.description: The Content-Type the object was stored with (may differ from the request if defaulted from the extension).

filename.description: Original basename of the upload (≤128 chars). For tracking only; not part of the URL path.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the bucket lifecycle rule will delete the object.

ttl_hours.description: TTL relative to upload time, in hours.

AssetPresignRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/upload_asset with `mode: "presign"` — the
path AI agents take (MCP can't carry binary). Server mints an S3 PUT
URL the caller uses directly. No bytes through this call.

filename.description: Original filename — used to pick the S3 extension (`.mp4`, `.mp3`, `.png`, …). Basename only; any path is stripped.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type. Used by the downstream pipeline only (informational) — NOT bound to the S3 signature, so the caller does NOT need to echo it back on the PUT.

AssetUploadJSONRequest.description:
Legacy / small-file JSON body — bytes inline as base64. Server cap
500 MB decoded; the MCP transport caps you to ~25 MB per call, so
agents take the `AssetPresignRequest` path instead.

file_data.description: Raw asset bytes, **base64-encoded**. No `data:...;base64,` prefix needed (silently stripped).

filename.description: Original filename — used to pick the on-disk extension (`.mp4`, `.mp3`, `.png`, …).

content_type.description: Optional MIME type (e.g. `audio/mpeg`, `video/mp4`, `image/jpeg`, `text/html`, `application/pdf`, `text/markdown`). Falls back to detection from the filename extension if omitted.

AssetPresignResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/upload_asset with `mode: "presign"`. The
caller PUTs the asset bytes to `put_url` (must echo back the
`headers_required` Content-Type), then uses `get_url` as their public
URL. `put_url` is valid for 1 hour; `get_url` resolves for 24 hours
after the PUT lands (bucket lifecycle).

put_url.description: Pre-signed S3 PUT URL. PUT your bytes here with the headers in `headers_required`. Valid for 1 hour.

get_url.description: Public S3 URL — pass into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or use as an inline `![](url)` in script_text.

headers_required.description:
Headers the caller MUST add to the PUT. Empty by design — the
signature only binds `host`, so `curl -X PUT --upload-file <file>
"<put_url>"` (no extra headers) works as-is across HTTP clients.

max_bytes.description: Hard server cap on the PUT body size, in bytes.

put_expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when `put_url` stops being accepted.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the bucket lifecycle rule will delete the object.

ttl_hours.description: TTL relative to upload time, in hours.

TelegramSendRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/telegram/send`. The recipient chat is resolved
server-side from the API key's company doc — there is no
`chat_id` / `to` field by design (prevents using WideCast as a
Telegram spam relay).

message.description:
Text body in plain-text mode, OR the caption when `photo_url` /
`video_url` is set. Telegram caps captions at 1024 bytes — the
server pre-validates and returns `message_too_long` (400) if
you exceed that in caption mode.

parse_mode.description:
Optional Telegram formatting mode. Omit for plain text. `HTML`
supports a small tag subset (b, i, u, s, code, pre, a); the
server strips other tags.

photo_url.description:
Optional photo to attach. Public http(s) URL — Telegram
downloads it server-side. Mutually exclusive with `video_url`.

video_url.description:
Optional video to attach. Public http(s) URL — Telegram
downloads it server-side. Mutually exclusive with `photo_url`.

TelegramMessageResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/telegram/send. `delivery` discriminates
which channel was used:
  * `telegram` → `chat_id_masked` + `telegram_message_id` are set,
    email-fallback fields are absent.
  * `email` → `recipient_email_masked`, `fallback_reason`, `setup_url`,
    and `note` are set; Telegram fields are absent.

delivery.description:
Which channel actually delivered the message. `telegram` when
the user has connected; `email` when they haven't (fallback).

chat_id_masked.description: Set only when `delivery="telegram"`. `…` + last 4 digits of the user's chat_id.

telegram_message_id.description: Set only when `delivery="telegram"`. Upstream Telegram message_id for later edit/delete.

recipient_email_masked.description: Set only when `delivery="email"`. Email of the account that received the fallback.

fallback_reason.description: Set only when `delivery="email"`. Why the fallback fired.

setup_url.description: Set only when `delivery="email"`. Send the user here to connect Telegram so future calls land in Telegram instead.

note.description: Set only when `delivery="email"`. Human-readable explanation the caller can relay to the user.

content.description:
What the content is created from: a URL, an idea/topic description,
or pasted text.

content_type.description:
What to write: `blog` (long-form), `facebook`, `x` (Twitter/X), or
`linkedin` post. Maps to the legacy content_type 3/4/5/6 internally.

callback_url.description: Optional HTTPS webhook for completion events.

metadata.description: Optional key-value pairs echoed back on /v1/status.

CreateContentRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/create_content. Async — returns a widecast* id +
`result.review_url` (the content viewer) in the create response itself
(share immediately; viewer shows a spinner). Poll GET /v1/status/{id}
until `completed` for the final state.

CreateImageRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/create_image. Charges 1 credit per image
generated (count=4 → 4 credits).

prompt.description:
Image description. Concrete visual nouns work better than
abstract concepts — "a wooden ladder against a red brick wall,
morning light" beats "climbing the corporate ladder".

count.description:
How many variations to generate in one call. Each = 1 credit.
Use `count=3..4` when the user wants options to pick from.

topic_id.description:
Optional. Link the generated image to an existing video's asset
folder so the scene editor can reuse it. Omit for freeform.

number.description: 1-based index — agents render a numbered thumbnail list keyed off this.

url.description: Public URL to the full-resolution image asset.

thumbnail_url.description: URL to use as the thumbnail (currently same as `url`).

status.description:
`completed` if every requested variant succeeded; `partial` if
some variants failed (see `error` + the surviving `images`).

keyword.description:
Search keyword (1-3 words work best). Pexels/Pixabay token-match
poorly with sentence-long queries — keep it tight.

kind.description:
What to search: `video` = stock CLIPS (Pexels/Pixabay/Shutterstock,
broll.js Stock tab); `image` = real PHOTOS (Google, broll.js
Photos tab).

ratio.description:
Orientation hint. Only filters when `kind == "video"`. Image
search ignores it (crop client-side if needed).

number.description: 1-based index — agents render a numbered thumbnail list keyed off this.

url.description: Public URL to the full-resolution asset.

context_url.description: Web page the image was crawled from (image results only).

VideoDataSegmentNarrator.description:
Narrator block on a scene segment (face/voice clone or recorded
media). All fields optional — populated only when the scene has a
narrator configured (A-roll, or B-roll that opted-in to voiceover).

VideoDataSegment.description: One scene/segment in the video_data response.

voice_file.description: Per-scene UID — pass as `value` with `by="voice_file"` to /v1/modify_scene.

text.description: Narration (what the narrator says on this scene).

mediaUrl.description: Currently-shown background or A-roll overlay asset URL.

brollUrl.description: Pure B-roll URL (may differ from mediaUrl when an A-roll overlay was added).

VideoDataGlobalSettings.description:
Compact global_settings block — only user-facing fields. Deeply
nested render-only knobs are NOT surfaced (use the dashboard if you
need them).

review_url.description: Scene-editor URL — opens this video in the dashboard's editor for review/edit.

product_service_input.description: Describe the product/service to brainstorm ideas from (≥ 10 chars).
product_service_input.example: A budgeting app for freelancers with tax estimates

user_location.description:
Where the user is based (city/state/country). Used as a hint; can
differ from `target_location` (a Vietnam-based agency may target
a US audience).

target_location.description:
**Required (semantically).** Audience market the videos should
target (city/state/country). Drives which local trends, sources,
and language are used. If you call without this AND the account
doesn't have one cached, the API returns **HTTP 200** with
`{object: "clarification", needs_input: "target_location", message: …}`
and DOES NOT charge a credit — relay the message to the user,
get their answer, then retry. Do NOT infer from chat context —
ask explicitly; the target market can differ from where the user
is based.

CollectIdeasRequest.description: Body for POST /v1/collect_ideas (synchronous → IdeasResponse OR Clarification).

ClarificationResponse.description:
Returned by endpoints that need an additional input from the user
before they can produce a result. The server returns HTTP 200 (NOT
an error) so AI agents can relay the prompt without surfacing it as
a failure. No credits are charged for this response. The endpoint
is safe to retry as soon as the named field is provided.

Currently emitted by:
  * POST /v1/collect_ideas — when `target_location` is missing AND
    the account has no cached target market.
  * POST /v1/modify_scene — when `by="text"` matches two or more
    scenes too closely; `candidates` carries the list to disambiguate
    with the user.

needs_input.description:
Name of the missing input field — match it against the request
schema. Set the value the user provides on this field and retry
the same endpoint.

message.description:
Prompt to relay to the user (in their language if appropriate).
Already explains what the field is, why it matters, and what
format to expect.
message.example: Which target market / audience location should these video ideas target? e.g. 'California, United States', 'Texas, US', or 'Vietnam'.

candidates.description:
Only set by /v1/modify_scene when `by="text"` is ambiguous. List
of scenes that matched the supplied text closely enough to be
plausible. Show the `text` previews to the user, then call
/v1/modify_scene again with `by="voice_file"` and the chosen
scene's `voice_file`.

PublishRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/publish. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `topic_id`, `text`,
or `video_url`.

topic_id.description:
Publish an existing WideCast video OR blog/social post (the id from
/v1/create_video or /v1/create_content). Article vs video is
auto-detected.

text.description: Arbitrary text to post (optionally with photo_urls).

video_url.description: A direct video file URL (mp4/mov/…) to download + publish. Requires `title`.

title.description: Caption/title. Required when `video_url` is given; optional override for `topic_id`.

platforms.description: Target platforms. Defaults to ALL connected platforms.

scheduled_date.description: Optional ISO date/time to schedule the post (with `timezone`).

PublishResponse.description:
Accepted-publish envelope (HTTP 202). Poll GET /v1/status/{id} with any
of `request_ids` for per-platform results.

request_ids.description: All upstream request_ids (an article spanning text+photo may return two).

platforms.description: Platforms the publish was dispatched to.

skipped.description: Platforms skipped (not connected / missing required config).

Status.description: Unified async-task status envelope returned by `create_video` and `get_status`.

topic_id.description:
Mirrors `id` 1:1. Exposed separately because the legacy `/checkProgress`
response and the scene-editor URL (`?topic_id=`) use this name —
clients can pick whichever field name reads more clearly.

type.description:
Resource type. `video` for create_video / enhance_script ids;
`content` for create_content (written blog/social — `details.status`
carries the blog_status stage: Queued / Processing / Researching /
Deep research completed / Checking media / Completed); `publish` when
polling a /v1/publish request_id (then `result.posts[]` carries
per-platform post URLs).

status.description:
* `pending` — id issued, worker hasn't written the topic row yet
  (race window, usually <2s). The server caches issued ids in memory
  for 10 minutes so polling clients never see 404 during this window.
* `processing` — topic row exists, worker is on it. Stays in this
  state for the ENTIRE run (the abroll worker doesn't increment
  `step` until the final flip — don't expect granular progress).
* `completed` — scenes ready for review. (`result.review_url` is already populated from earlier states too — the completion signal is `stage` + `result.script`, not `review_url`.)
* `failed` — unrecoverable error (`error.code` + `error.message` populated).

stage.description: Fine-grained internal stage (informational, may evolve — don't gate logic on it).

progress.description:
Honest progress estimate (not step-based, since the worker stays at
step=0 for most of the run):
  * 0.05 — id issued, no topic row yet (pending / race)
  * 0.30 — topic row exists, no rendered script yet (worker starting)
  * 0.80 — script with segments present, finalisation pending
  * 1.00 — completed

skill_hint.description:
Informational nudge present on the `POST /v1/create_video` response
(NOT on `/v1/status` polls) when the supplied `script_text` looks
like the caller skipped `widecast_get_writing_skill` — e.g. no
inline `![alt](url)` markdown and no raw image/video URLs anywhere
in the script. The render still proceeds (auto-B-roll fills the
gap); this just teaches the AI to fetch the writing method next
time. The method is vendor-neutral — applies to any LLM.
skill_hint.example: script_text contains no inline media URLs. WideCast's writing method recommends …

progress_hint.description:
UX-friendly sub-stage label derived from elapsed time (NOT from real
worker state). Present only while `status == "processing"`. Polling
AIs should relay `progress_hint.label` to the user every poll to
keep the wait feeling alive. The label includes an ETA suffix in
English (e.g. "Generating scene visuals · ~7 min left") — the AI is
expected to translate to the user's language. Pseudo-progress: the
stage may not exactly match what the worker is doing internally.

details.description:
Fine-grained worker state surfaced from the legacy topic / queue row.
`null` during the pending race window (no topic row yet). For abroll
(current pilot endpoint), most fields stay at default until the
worker flips to step=5+Completed at the end; the render pipeline
(future endpoint) will populate these progressively.

usage.description:
Cost & credit info. **`null` in pilot** — populated once billing
lands (ROADMAP Phase 1).

StatusResult.description:
Minimal user-facing output. The v0.1.0 pilot returns `review_url` for
every completed video (auth-adaptive: read-only embeddable player when
not signed in, full editor when signed in), and additionally `video_url`
when the video was created with `output_type: "video"` (or when
`/v1/export_video` finished). The rendered video script (with
segments) is intentionally NOT inlined to keep status responses cheap.
A future `GET /v1/videos/{id}/script` endpoint will serve the full
script explicitly when needed.

review_url.description:
URL where the end user views / edits the rendered scenes + audio.
Append **`&readonly=true`** to get a public, **read-only player**
(no sign-in) that does NOT block iframe embedding — use that variant
as an `<iframe>` src to show the result inline. The plain URL opens
the full editor for a signed-in user. Keyed by `topic_id`
(+ `company_id`). Default template:
`https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=<id>` (overridable
server-side via `WIDECAST_REVIEW_URL_TEMPLATE` env); embeddable
variant: `https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=<id>&readonly=true`.

video_url.description:
Direct URL to the rendered MP4. Populated only for videos created
with `output_type: "video"` or exported via `POST /v1/export_video`.

ProgressHint.description:
Time-based pseudo-progress for UX during the 15-min create_video render
(and ~3-min export_video encode). Derived in the server from elapsed
time since the id was issued — NOT from real worker state — so the
stage label may not exactly match what the worker is doing internally.
Good enough for "show the user something" UX; not for gating logic.

Polling AIs should relay `label` to the user verbatim (translating to
the user's language as needed). `remaining_ms_estimate` is provided
separately for clients that want to format ETA differently than the
baked English "· ~N min left" suffix in `label`.

stage.description:
Machine-readable sub-stage key. Stable for code; not for display.
The set varies by what's running:
  * `create_video` `output_type=video` (full pipeline, ~15 min):
    queued / research / script / segmentation / voice_gen /
    image_gen / broll_fetch / composition / encoding / uploading
  * `create_video` `output_type=scene` (stops at scene editor, ~3 min):
    queued / research / script / segmentation / finalizing
  * `create_video` `output_type=text` (media-source Remake, ~3 min):
    queued / ingest / transcribe / script
  * `export_video` (post-review MP4 render, ~3 min):
    preparing / encoding_video / encoding_audio / muxing / uploading

label.description:
Human-readable English label with ETA suffix appended. Format:
`"<Sentence> · ~N min left"` (or `· Almost done` near the end).

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds since the id was issued.

remaining_ms_estimate.description:
Estimated milliseconds until completion (best-effort, ≥15 sec floor).
Drifts off if the worker is faster or slower than the typical timing.

ProcessingDetails.description:
Raw worker state for fine-grained progress visibility. Field names
mirror the legacy `topics_table` (or `video_queue_table`) schema.

⚠ **DELIBERATE NAME CLASH**: `details.status` is a free-form legacy
string ("Completed", "Error", "Avatar videos downloaded", …),
DISTINCT from the top-level `status` enum. Gate logic on the
top-level value; treat `details.status` as a human/debug hint.

step.description: Legacy `step` value (0 during abroll, 5 at completion). Render pipeline cycles 0→2→5.

status.description: Free-form legacy state string. NOT our top-level status enum.

notes.description: Free-form note from the worker (errors, assignment messages, etc.).

updated_at.description: When the worker last touched the row (ISO 8601 UTC).

input_truncated_from.description:
Original word count when the server auto-truncated a generative
input to its max (idea_text → 1000, blog_text → 3000). Only
present when the input exceeded the bound. Lets clients show
"your 4200-word article was trimmed to 3000 words" UX hints.

ListEnvelope.description:
**Pagination convention** for every future list endpoint.
Cursor-based — no list endpoint in v0.1.0 yet; this schema is reserved.

WebhookEvent.description:
The payload WideCast POSTs to your `callback_url`. Headers:
  * `User-Agent: WideCast-Webhook/<version>`
  * `X-WideCast-Event: <event_id>`
  * `X-WideCast-Event-Type: <event_type>`
  * `X-WideCast-Signature: t=<unix_ts>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex>` — verify against `WIDECAST_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
  * `X-WideCast-Delivery: <uuid>` — unique per delivery attempt
  * `X-WideCast-Attempt: <n>` — 1-indexed retry counter

Retry: 10 attempts spread across 24h (offsets 0s/1m/5m/15m/30m/1h/3h/6h/12h/24h).
Acknowledge with HTTP 2xx within 30s; non-2xx triggers retry until
success, abandon (4xx), exhaustion (10 attempts), or 24h timeout.

event_id.description: Unique per event — dedupe on this in your handler.

event_type.description:
* `video.processing` — fires once, immediately after `POST /v1/create_video` (server has accepted, worker spawned).
* `video.completed` — fires once, when status first reaches `completed`. `data.result.review_url` populated.
* `video.failed` — fires once, when status first reaches `failed`. `data.error.{code,message}` populated.

details.description:
Code-specific structured data. Currently populated for
`code == "credit_exhausted"` and `code == "account_expired"`
(HTTP 402) — see `CreditErrorDetails`. Other error codes
leave this `null`.

CreditErrorDetails.description:
Structured upgrade / wait info attached to HTTP 402 responses
(`credit_exhausted` or `account_expired`). AI clients should surface
both options to the user — wait until the next monthly reset
(`reset_at`) OR upgrade now via `upgrade_url` — rather than only
relaying the prose `message`.

upgrade_url.description: Pricing page where the user can upgrade their plan.

reset_at.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the user's current period ends and the
quota refreshes. Sourced from `system_configs.valid_to` — same
field that drives the `account_expired` gate (interpretation flips
based on whether `valid_to` is past or future relative to now).
Present for `credit_exhausted`; absent for `account_expired`.

expired_at.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the paid plan expired.
Present for `account_expired`; absent for `credit_exhausted`.

renew_url.description:
Where the user renews an expired plan. Present for
`account_expired`; identical to `upgrade_url` in practice.

current_plan_quota.description: Monthly credit allocation on the user's current plan.

credits_remaining.description: Credits left in the user's current monthly allocation.

credits_required.description: Credits this operation would have consumed.

next_plan.description:
Suggested next plan to upgrade to (one tier above current).
`null` when the user is already on the top tier (Enterprise).

next_plan_quota.description: Monthly credit allocation on the suggested next plan.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, malformed, or revoked API key. Send a valid key as
`Authorization: Bearer wc_live_...`. `error.code` is `missing_api_key`
(no key) or `invalid_api_key` (malformed / unknown / revoked);
`error.type` is `authentication_error`.

PaymentRequired.description:
The account cannot be charged for this operation — `error.code` is
`credit_exhausted` (out of credits) or `account_expired`. The
response carries an `error.details` object (see `CreditErrorDetails`)
with the upgrade URL, next monthly reset, and current/next plan info
so AI clients can format a "wait vs upgrade" choice for the user
instead of just relaying the prose message.

PreconditionFailed.description:
The request is well-formed but the resource is not in the expected
state — e.g. trying to export a video whose scenes are not yet
ready (`error.code = "scenes_not_ready"`).
